# Specification Review Checklist: Repository Quality Gate and Plugin Packaging

**Purpose**: Validate the quality of the requirements themselves — completeness, clarity, internal consistency, and testability — before planning turns them into design decisions
**Created**: 2026-09-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for all five content kinds named in FR-001, with none of them left implicit? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the documented location of each committed configuration specified, or only that one must exist? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for the order in which the aggregate command runs its checks, given that FR-007 makes the order observable? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec state what the fallback mechanism itself is permitted to require of the machine running it, beyond the exclusion in FR-010? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK005 Are requirements defined for how the written record in FR-014 is located and kept in step with the configurations it explains? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the required fields of the plugin declaration in FR-016 specified, or is "recognised under the name" the whole requirement? [Completeness, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec define what "machine-local and agent-local state" covers in FR-018, independently of the exclusion list in FR-013? [Clarity, Spec §FR-018]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "the same verdict" in FR-008 defined precisely enough to be disputed — does it cover exit status, violation set, and violation ordering? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK009 Is "where the content type has line granularity" in FR-006 decidable per content kind, or does it leave the reporting obligation ambiguous? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "an explicit fix flag" in FR-012 specified as a named flag, or left to implementation to choose? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "no automatic fix available" in FR-012a determinable from the requirements, or does it depend on facts the spec does not state? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012a]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "any dependency directory fetched rather than authored" in FR-013 a criterion a reader can apply without judgement calls? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "departs from the tool's documented default" in FR-014 well defined for a setting the tool documents no default for? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "no prior setup" in SC-001 consistent with the container-runtime prerequisite the Assumptions section permits? [Clarity, Spec §SC-001]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK015 Do FR-005 and FR-011 agree on exit status semantics, given that both mandate non-zero for materially different reasons? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK016 Do FR-007 and FR-011 agree on whether the aggregate command's stop is the same stop in both cases? [Consistency, Spec §FR-007, §FR-011]
- [ ] CHK017 Do FR-012 and FR-005 agree on the exit status of a fix invocation that successfully rewrote files — is that a pass or a fail? [Conflict, Spec §FR-005, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK018 Do FR-013 and FR-017 agree, given that FR-017 requires the scripts be checked while FR-013 excludes generated content and the scripts are authored? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-017]
- [ ] CHK019 Does FR-018 duplicate part of FR-013's exclusion set, and if so is the overlap intentional and consistent? [Consistency, Spec §FR-013, §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK020 Do the Assumptions section and FR-004 agree on how many entry points exist, and does the spec name both consistently throughout? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the terminology consistent across the spec — "check", "command", "aggregate command", "entry point" — or are these synonyms for the same entity? [Terminology, Spec §Key Entities]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK022 Can SC-001 be objectively measured, given that "with no documentation reading beyond the command's name" describes a reader's state of mind? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK023 Is SC-003's "0 differences" measurable without specifying how the two machine states are established? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK024 Is SC-004's "100% coverage" verifiable given CHK013's question about settings with no documented default? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]
- [ ] CHK025 Does SC-006's "without human interpretation of its output" state a checkable outcome? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK026 Is SC-008 verifiable as written, or does it require a list of which file types are governed by more than one check? [Measurability, Spec §SC-008]
- [ ] CHK027 Does every acceptance scenario in User Stories 1–4 state an observable outcome rather than an internal one? [Acceptance Criteria, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK028 Is a requirement and acceptance-criteria ID scheme established and used consistently across FR, SC, and the user stories? [Traceability]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK029 Are requirements defined for the primary flow of every user story, or do any stories rest only on success criteria? [Coverage, Spec §User Scenarios]
- [ ] CHK030 Are exception-flow requirements defined for a fix invocation that fails partway, leaving some files rewritten and others not? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK031 Are recovery requirements defined for a fix invocation whose rewrites the contributor wants to undo? [Gap, Recovery Flow]
- [ ] CHK032 Are requirements defined for the flow where a check's configuration file is itself missing or malformed? [Gap, Exception Flow]
- [ ] CHK033 Are requirements defined for the plugin-installation failure flow beyond the single scenario in User Story 4? [Coverage, Spec §User Story 4]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK034 Are the five edge cases listed in the spec each traceable to a functional requirement that governs them? [Traceability, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK035 Are requirements defined for a file that is in scope by FR-013 but that no content standard in FR-001 governs? [Gap, Coverage]
- [ ] CHK036 Are requirements defined for the case where the installed tool and the fallback would disagree, rather than one being absent? [Gap, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK037 Is the empty-input-set case in the Edge Cases section reconciled with FR-005's exit-status rule? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK038 Are any requirements stated for how long the aggregate check may take, or is duration deliberately unconstrained? [Gap, Non-Functional]
- [ ] CHK039 Are requirements defined for the trustworthiness of the fallback mechanism's inputs, given FR-008's reproducibility claim? [Gap, Security]
- [ ] CHK040 Are observability requirements defined — what a reader can tell from output about which path a check took? [Gap, Observability]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK041 Is each of the six assumptions in the Assumptions section traceable to a functional requirement or explicitly marked as scope-limiting only? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK042 Is the assumption that "the checks are the repository's tests" consistent with the constitution's requirement that the aggregate check pass before review? [Consistency, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK043 Is the container-runtime assumption validated, or asserted — does the spec state what happens for a contributor who cannot install one? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK044 Are the five Out of Scope entries each unambiguous enough to settle a future "is this in scope?" question? [Clarity, Spec §Out of Scope]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK045 Do the three resolved clarifications leave any downstream requirement still phrased against the pre-clarification reading? [Consistency, Spec §Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK046 Does any requirement still contain an unquantified adjective — "clear", "predictable", "plain", "immediate", "unambiguous"? [Ambiguity]
- [ ] CHK047 Is the relationship between FR-002 and FR-013a clear, given that both require configuration to be committed but for different things? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002, §FR-013a]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Focus areas: requirements completeness, clarity, internal consistency, testability of acceptance criteria. Depth: standard. Audience: reviewer, before planning.
- CHK017 and CHK018 are the two items most likely to surface a real conflict rather than a wording gap; if either fails, the spec needs amending before `plan` reads it.
- CHK017 outcome (recorded by the implementation run, checkbox left for the reviewer): the conflict was
  real and has been resolved in the spec. FR-005 alone left a successful fix run's exit status
  undefined, because a run that found violations and repaired them satisfies both "violations were
  found" and "the tree now conforms". FR-005a was added to settle it: a fix invocation that rewrote
  files into conformance exits `0`. Verified against the code — `scripts/lint-format.sh --fix` on a
  deliberately misformatted file rewrites it and exits `0`.
- CHK018 outcome (recorded by the implementation run, checkbox left for the reviewer): no conflict.
  FR-013 excludes _generated_ and agent-local content; the runner scripts are authored content and
  are in scope, so FR-017 is satisfied without weakening FR-013. Verified by enumeration: 11 files
  under `scripts/` are in the shell check's file list, and `scripts/lint-shell.sh` reports zero
  findings on them.
